newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel steady, Russian cargoes sell.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel steady, Russian cargoes sell.

text.p: NWE low sulphur straight-run was stable to slightly weaker in thin trade while Russian high sulphur was generating good interest on Thursday, traders said.
Low sulphur prices slipped $1 to $101/$103 fob in Europe with some material heard on offer for early April.
Two 10kt low sulphur pieces were heard traded inland UK at close to $110 cif.

Trade in Russian high sulphur straight-run has been brisk for the last weeks, with cargoes being snapped up as they appear in the Baltic ports. E-4 premiums were reported holding steady around $3-$5, depending on quality.
A small cargo of E-4 was heard traded on Wednesday at three means +$5.75, with freight accounting for the extra cost, dealers said.

An M-40 cargo from Klaipeda with 1.7 percent maximum water content was heard bought on Wednesday by a major for two means +$8.50. On the same day a trader bought an M-100 cargo from a distressed seller for two means +$3.
Traders were speculating that appetite for Russian fuel would weaken if high premiums persist and crude's weakness continues.
"The equation is turning around now. The economics of refining straight-run were attractive but are less so right now," said one trader.

One 40,000 tonne E-4 cargo, loading 8-9/4 in Ventspils, heard offered at a premium of less than $4, had not been taken. Some said that reflected market softness, others that the cargo size made it difficult to handle.

In the Mediterranean, Russian straight-run cargoes that could not go into Italian refineries because of maintenance, and were expected to weigh on the market, were reported to have largely found homes.
An M-40 cargo that had been looking for an owner for some days was heard sold to Spanish refiner Cepsa.
But further Black Sea supplies were in the offing for mid-April that might weaken prices in the medium term.
